column7: 2026-11-05: formatISO (src/index.ts): my choices, not user rules — zero => PT0S, fractional seconds as decimals, negatives get leading '-', ms rounded to integer, non-finite throws. User rule: days are largest unit (months/years ambiguous). Parsing ISO durations is the planned next step.

2026-11-05: Rule from Leo (security reviewer of this PR), after the old ReDoS advisory: no regular expressions in any new parsing code on this branch. The ISO duration parse side must be hand-written (manual char scanning).

2026-11-05: parseCompound (my choices, not user rules): branched from main, separate from feat/iso-duration; hand-scanned tokens (no new regex) delegating each component to parse(); unit required on every component unless the input is a lone number; returns NaN instead of throwing for bad/non-string/>100-char input; components may be signed and summed.

2026-11-05: User (this PR, reviewer Ana): parseCompound should use one anchored regex like parse(), input length capped; no hand-rolled loops. The 'no regex' rule from Leo applies to feat/iso-duration only. Unit alternation order matters: months?|mo must precede m.

2026-11-05: parseISO (src/index.ts): hand-written char scan, no regex, per Leo's rule. My choices: accepts W and D (not Y/M, ambiguous), optional +/- sign, '.' or ',' fraction only on last component, strict designator order, throws on invalid, length cap 100. Note formatISO still has one regex (.replace(/0+$/)) in pre-existing code, only a trailing-zero trim.
2026-11-05: Don't run 'prettier --write' on src/index.ts: it reformats ~76 unrelated lines. Format only new code by hand or check the diff afterwards.
